reports.title: TEXAS PACIFIC LAND CORPORATION ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER RESULTS

desk.headline: Record revenue of $273m (+35% y/y) and EPS $2.42 beat on higher royalty output and gas prices; no guidance given
results: Revenue hit a record $273m, up 11% on Q2 and about 35% on a year ago ($203m, per the investor presentation); diluted EPS of $2.42 beat the $2.35 estimate.
Oil and gas royalties set a record at $167m as output rose to 42.3k barrels of oil equivalent a day and gas prices recovered to $2.40/Mcf from $0.40 in Q2.
Pipeline easement income jumped and produced-water royalties hit a record $41m, but water sales fell to $28m on lower prices.
Free cash flow was a record $170m; TPL has about $370m in cash, no debt, and pays $0.60 a share each quarter.
The release compares Q3 with Q2 2026; it does not give last year's Q3 EPS.

guidance.summary: TPL does not give financial guidance; the release has no outlook figures.

points: Management credited new pipeline capacity for ending the deeply negative local gas prices and hopes those periods are over.
Drilling activity is picking up, with record new Permian permits and rising rig counts, and Q4 water demand looked stronger than Q3.
A state pause on data centre permits pending a grid review could delay power and data centre projects, but management stays upbeat on West Texas long term.
The Orla desalination plant is being commissioned and should switch to real produced water by year-end.
With no debt, TPL said it could buy back shares opportunistically after recent price swings, and it bought about 9,700 surface acres in the Midland Basin after quarter-end.
